Turkey has quota rules distinct from chicken and eggs — including a class of quota that can’t be transferred at all. If you’re buying or selling a turkey farm in BC, start here.
How does turkey quota transfer in BC?
Turkey quota is administered by the
may only be transferred on application by both the transferor and transferee, with the Board’s written approval — and the Board can impose conditions or refuse a transfer for several reasons.

Quota does not simply run with the land. Any transfer must be applied for by both parties and approved by the applicable marketing board, and it isn’t included in a sale unless expressly stated in the Contract of Purchase and Sale.
What is secondary turkey quota — and can I buy it?

That’s an important distinction when valuing a turkey operation: only the primary quota can move to a buyer, subject to Board approval. Make sure any purchase clearly identifies which quota is primary and transferable.
Why can a turkey quota transfer be refused?
. The Board can decline a transfer if the buyer doesn’t have adequate room in their Turkey Production Unit to accommodate the production tied to the quota. That makes
central to whether a deal can even proceed — not just to its price.
